Content.1. Mentoring is most effective when it c: Primary focus: Research (study design, grant writing, publication strategy). Secondary focus: Leadership and career development (team management, building a research group, academic promotion).
Content.2. Within each area, what specific guida: Research: skill acquisition in grant writing (R-series applications), study design and statistical planning, manuscript preparation and target journal selection, building collaborations, and developing a clear research niche. Leadership/career development: guidance on hiring and managing personnel, delegating tasks, building a lab culture, preparing promotion materials (CV, teaching/mentoring dossiers), negotiation for protected time, time management strategies to maintain work–life balance, and introductions to potential collaborators and national networks.
Content.3. Career development goals-What does th: 3 years: Establish a funded independent pilot portfolio (K-award or equivalent), publish first independent papers, recruit 1–2 trainees, and secure 20–30% protected research time. 5 years: Obtain a major independent grant (R01 or equivalent), be promoted to Associate Professor (or equivalent), lead a multidisciplinary team, and develop a distinct research program with sustained productivity. 10 years: Achieve national recognition in the field, maintain continuous major funding, hold a departmental or center leadership role, mentor multiple successful junior investigators, and translate research findings into clinical impact or implemented practice change.
